name: a split marker with its ratio from the record
spec: docs/architecture.md §18, splits from the record: a ratio applies to a marker that states no quantity; the cost stays
working: 100 X bought for 1,000; a 2-for-1 split; 200 sold for 1,200: P&L 200; entry 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5; marked split

name: a consolidation under a new security id, stated as units out and in: the holding continues
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, corporate events: the broker's units stand; a whole holding continuing under another instrument keeps its round trip, cost and dates
working: 100 of the old listing bought for 1,000
the event: 100 out of the old, 20 into the new (one for five); the round trip continues on the new listing with cost 1,000
20 sold for 1,200: P&L 200, one trade opened by the first purchase, named after the new listing

name: a stock dividend is income, and its value is the new units' cost
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, Corporate events: a stock dividend's value is income and becomes the units' cost
working: 100 X bought for 1,000; 5 units paid as a dividend worth 60
a dividend row of 60 in the cashflow; 105 sold for 1,260: P&L 1,260 − 1,000 − 60 = 200

name: a spin-off with two children: each takes its share of the parent's cost as it stood, and the parent's dates
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, Corporate events: the parent's cost is split, the child's lots keep the parent's acquisition dates
working: 100 P bought for 1,000 (Jan 5); the event: 50 C and 20 D received, C taking 20 % of the cost and D 10 %
C's cost 1,000 × 0.2 = 200, D's 1,000 × 0.1 = 100, both of the cost before the event; P keeps 700
50 C sold for 300 (Apr 1): P&L 100, held from Jan 5 → 86 days; 100 P sold for 900: P&L 200; D held, 20 at 100

name: a merger for cash closes the holding at the cash per unit
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, corporate events: a merger for cash
working: 100 X bought for 1,000; merged for 15 a unit: closed at 1,500, P&L 500

name: an event nothing says the kind of: the units the broker states move at an unknown cost, and the holding waits
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md: an event without an adjustment moves the units the broker states and leaves the holding waiting
working: 100 X bought for 1,000; 100 more arrive by an event with no values; 200 sold for 3,000: the P&L waits (event-unknown)

name: a short through a split: the short is scaled by the ratio, its proceeds kept
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, corporate events: a split or a continuation by its ratio scales or moves a short as it does a long; any other event on a short leaves the holding waiting
working: 100 X sold short (to open) for +1,000; a 2-for-1 split: a short of 200, entry 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5
200 bought back for −800: P&L 1,000 − 800 = 200, marked split

name: a short through a continuation under a new instrument: the short moves whole by the ratio
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, corporate events: a split or a continuation by its ratio scales or moves a short as it does a long; any other event on a short leaves the holding waiting
working: 100 OLD sold short (to open) for +1,000; OLD continues as NEW, one for five: a short of 20 NEW, its round trip and proceeds kept
20 NEW bought back for −800: P&L 200, one trade opened by the short sale, named after NEW

name: a stock dividend on a short: what the short owes is not worked out, and the holding waits
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, corporate events: a split or a continuation by its ratio scales or moves a short as it does a long; any other event on a short leaves the holding waiting
working: 100 X sold short (to open) for +1,000; a stock dividend of 0.05 new units per unit valued at 50: the short owes the lender those units, which the ledger does not work out
the event is not applied; the short of 100 waits on it
